[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Active Support Instrumentation and Notifications in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Active Support is a core component of Ruby on Rails that provides utility classes and standard library extensions. One of its most powerful features for application monitoring and performance tuning is the Instrumentation API (ActiveSupport::Notifications)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding ActiveSupport::Notifications"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The instrumentation system allows developers to hook into specific events within their application. It operates on a publish-subscribe pattern, where code blocks publish events, and subscribers listen to those events to log data, track performance metrics, or trigger analytics."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Instrumenting Custom Code"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To measure the execution time and capture metadata of a specific block of code, use the `ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument` method. You provide a name for the event and a hash of payload data."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"class PaymentGateway
  def process(amount, user)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("process_payment.payment_gateway", amount: amount, user_id: user.id) do
      # Perform actual payment processing logic here
      gateway_api_call(amount)
    end
  end
end"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Subscribing to Events"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To listen to events published by your application, you must register a subscriber using `ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe`. This is typically done during application initialization, such as in an initializer file like `config/initializers/instrumentation.rb`."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("process_payment.payment_gateway") do |name, started, finished, unique_id, payload|
  duration = (finished - started) * 1000 # duration in milliseconds
  Rails.logger.info "Event: #{name} | User: #{payload[:user_id]} | Amount: #{payload[:amount]} | Duration: #{duration.round(2)}ms"
end"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Event Objects"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Instead of parsing individual block arguments in your subscriber, you can pass an instance of `ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event`. This provides convenient helper methods like `duration`, `time`, and `payload`."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("process_payment.payment_gateway") do |*args|
  event = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
  
  Rails.logger.info "Processed payment in #{event.duration}ms with status success"
end"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Instrumentation"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Namespace your event names using dot notation (e.g., action.object, such as render.action_view)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep payloads light to avoid memory bloat; pass IDs and small primitives rather than massive ActiveRecord objects when possible."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Wrap risky or slow third-party API calls with instrumentation to accurately track performance bottlenecks in production."}]
